intro: Hands-on terminal exam: about 17 tasks on live clusters, 120 min, pass 66%, USD 445, two attempts, includes two killer.sh simulator sessions. Here the quiz and the mock exam are the same hands-on tasks: you type the commands you would run and Claude grades them. The playbook below is what to practise in a real terminal.

playbook.problem: A pod is not running (Pending, CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, Error)

commands.what: Status, restarts, which node. -o wide adds node and IP.
Read the Events at the bottom first: scheduling, image pull, probe failures live there.
Logs of the container that just crashed. Add -c <container> for multi-container pods.
Events for the whole namespace in time order.

commands.cmd: kubectl get nodes; kubectl describe node <node>
commands.what: Conditions (MemoryPressure, DiskPressure, Ready) and the kubelet message.

commands.cmd: ssh <node>; sudo systemctl status kubelet; sudo journalctl -u kubelet -f
commands.what: systemctl shows if the service runs; journalctl -u follows that unit's log.
Start the kubelet now and on every boot.
Static pod manifests and the containers the runtime actually runs.

playbook.problem: A Service does not reach its pods

commands.what: If ENDPOINTS is empty, the selector does not match the pod labels.
Compare the labels with the service selector.
A throwaway pod that curls the service by DNS name. --rm deletes it when it exits.
A NetworkPolicy may be blocking the traffic.

playbook.problem: Create or change a workload fast (imperative first, then YAML)

commands.what: --dry-run=client prints the object without creating it; -o yaml gives you a file to edit.
Deployment in one line. Add --dry-run=client -o yaml to get a manifest.
Service from a Deployment. --port is the service port, --target-port the container port.

commands.cmd: kubectl set image deployment/api api=nginx:1.28; kubectl rollout status deployment/api; kubectl rollout undo deployment/api
commands.what: Update the image, watch the rollout, roll back.

commands.cmd: kubectl scale deployment api --replicas=5; kubectl autoscale deployment api --min=2 --max=8 --cpu-percent=70
commands.what: Manual scale and an HPA.
Opens the live YAML in vim. :wq saves and applies; a failed apply drops a tmp file path you can fix.

commands.cmd: kubectl get deployment api -o yaml > api.yaml; vim api.yaml; kubectl apply -f api.yaml
commands.what: Safer for big edits. Pods cannot change most fields: delete and recreate (kubectl replace --force -f pod.yaml).
Field documentation offline. Use it instead of guessing YAML keys.

commands.cmd: kubectl label node <node> disktype=ssd; kubectl taint node <node> key=value:NoSchedule
commands.what: Labels attract (nodeSelector/affinity), taints repel unless a pod tolerates them. Remove a taint with a trailing minus: key=value:NoSchedule-

commands.cmd: kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data; kubectl uncordon <node>
commands.what: Node maintenance: stop scheduling, evict pods, allow again.
A Role is namespaced; ClusterRole is cluster-wide.
Bind the role to a ServiceAccount (or --user=jane).
Verify as that identity. Answers yes or no.
The three cert flags come from the etcd static pod manifest (kubectl describe pod etcd-<node> -n kube-system).
Restore into a new directory, then point the etcd manifest's hostPath at it.

commands.cmd: kubectl drain <cp> --ignore-daemonsets; sudo apt-get install -y kubeadm=1.3x.y-*; sudo kubeadm upgrade plan; sudo kubeadm upgrade apply v1.3x.y
commands.what: Control plane: drain, upgrade kubeadm, plan, apply.

commands.cmd: sudo apt-get install -y kubelet=1.3x.y-* kubectl=1.3x.y-*; sudo systemctl daemon-reload; sudo systemctl restart kubelet; kubectl uncordon <cp>
commands.what: Then kubelet and kubectl, restart, uncordon. Workers: kubeadm upgrade node instead of apply.
Status Bound means the PVC found a PV. Pending means no PV matches size, access mode or storageClassName.
Events say why it is not binding.
Ingress in one line; add --annotation for rewrites.
Gateway API objects (new curriculum).
DNS check from inside a pod.

commands.cmd: alias k=kubectl; export do='--dry-run=client -o yaml'; export now='--force --grace-period=0'
commands.what: Type k run x --image=nginx $do > x.yaml. The aliases save minutes.

commands.cmd: kubectl config use-context <ctx>; kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=<ns>
commands.what: Every task tells you the context. Switch first, then set the default namespace.

commands.cmd: grep -n <text> file; sed -i 's/old/new/' file; tail -f /var/log/x; cat file | less
commands.what: grep finds a line (-n shows the number), sed -i edits in place, tail -f follows a growing log.

commands.cmd: echo "text" > file (overwrite); echo "more" >> file (append); cmd1 | cmd2 (pipe output into input)
commands.what: The three redirections you will use most.

commands.cmd: kubectl get pods -A -o json | jq '.items[].metadata.name'; kubectl get pods -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,NODE:.spec.nodeName
commands.what: Pull specific fields when a task asks you to write names to a file.
